CHAPTER IV
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
Part One
Institutional Arrangements

Article 18
(1) Regional governments are obligated to conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

Article 9
(1) In the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence which includes prevention and mitigation activities, an Integrated Service Center (PPT) shall be established.
(2) The PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of elements from the Regional Government and elements originating from related institutions outside the Regional Government.
(3) Further provisions regarding the PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be further regulated by Mayor Regulation.
(4) The PPT as referred to in Paragraph (1), in implementing protection for women and children victims of violence may conduct coordination with institutions and or organizations in Tual City.
(5) In the Implementation of Protection for women and children victims of violence, it may be established at the sub-district, urban village and village levels.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Tual.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and Co-Administration with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Mayor is the Mayor of Tual.
5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution as an element of Regional Government administration.
6. Implementation is all actions carried out by government and non-government institutions which include prevention, protection and recovery for victims of violence against women and children.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, and is not yet married including a child still in the womb.
8. Woman is every person who is physically born as a woman.
9. Victim is a woman and or child who experiences suffering and or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Prevention is all efforts carried out by government and non-government institutions aimed at providing a sense of security to women and children.
11. Child protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Women protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Suffering is any act that results in or can result in suffering whether psychological, physical, sexual, economic, social to the victim.
14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting or causes death.
15. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling afraid of helplessness, and or severe psychological suffering to women and or children.
16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
17. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim, when seeing, hearing and knowing of, during or after the occurrence of violence against the victim.
18. Companion is a person or institution that has the ability to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy, legal services and advocacy for strengthening victim recovery.
19. Women and child protection institution is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (Including Medicolegal), psycho-social and legal services.
20. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to women and children victims in accordance with the standard operating procedures or abbreviated as SOP that are determined.
21. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or other community organizations.
22. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a unified unit that organizes integrated service functions for women and children victims of violence, based in hospitals, community health centers, P2TP2A, Safe Houses, Child Social Protection Houses (RPSA), Trauma Center Protection Houses (RPTC), Women's Social Protection Houses (RPSW).
23. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence in a comprehensive and quality manner.

CHAPTER VI
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 15
(1) The Government in implementing protection for women and children victims of violence may involve community participation.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1), may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

I. GENERAL
The implementation of protection for victims of violence is carried out based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. So that every person must obtain their right to protection against a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of just and civilized humanity. In principle, the strategic target of implementing protection is to maintain the sustainability of protection through integrated, comprehensive services and safe and comfortable shelters that are conducive for victims of violence. These strategic targets are pursued through interrelated stages, including planning, protection, services and financing, supervision and sanctions.
Therefore, a legal umbrella is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation that is capable of accommodating all issues related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, capable of providing integrated services in a holistic and comprehensive manner, and explicitly providing a mandate to institutions to carry out policy coordination and supervision, and a mandate to institutions to provide services. In addition, regional regulations can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community to play a broad role.
Based on several considerations above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER V
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
Article 12
(1) Forms of violence against women and children include physical, psychological, sexual, neglect, exploitation and other violence.
(2) Forms of physical violence are any acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage of a fetus in the womb and or cause death.
(3) Forms of sexual violence are sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes or certain purposes.
(4) Forms of psychological violence are acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness.
(5) Forms of violence through neglect are intentional or unintentional actions that result in the non-fulfillment of basic needs.
(6) Forms of violence through exploitation are forms of violence including acts of exploiting children economically or sexually to benefit oneself or others, actions with or without the consent of the victim but not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully, transferring or transplanting organs and or body tissues or exploiting or the ability of a person to obtain benefits.

Article 16
(1) Social Community Organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in article 15 paragraph (2), shall be given guidance by the regional government through regional apparatus organizations related to the duties of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Organizational guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 11
(1) The implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner in medical treatment, legal protection, medicolegal, psychological and economic aspects, the implementation of which can be conducted through partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the protection of women and children.
(2) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), must take into account religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(3) Principles of service and assistance:
c. fast, safe and empathetic;
d. guarantee of confidentiality;
e. easily accessible; and
f. free of charge.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1), is implemented in accordance with standard operating procedures.

2.1.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation clearly establishes an institutional coordination mechanism/network for service delivery: Pasal 9 forms a Pusat Pelayanan Terpadu (PPT) consisting of elements of the local government and related institutions outside the local government ("terdiri dari unsur Pemerintah Daerah dan unsur ... di luar Pemerintah Daerah") and explicitly allows coordination with institutions/organizations ("dapat melakukan koordinasi dengan lembaga dan atau organisasi di Kota Tual"). Pasal 10 also allows forming P2TP2A with multi-sector membership (police, prosecutor, court, health, social, ministry of religion, NGOs, etc.) and coordination/partnership with PPT. These provisions satisfy an 'institutional network/coordination mechanism' indicator even if they are not cross-jurisdictional. The retrieved English passages contained this same information, but the judge incorrectly required coordination 'across different jurisdictions' and therefore answered No.
